whispered she. <break time="0.8s" /> Softly and rather sadly. <break time="0.8s" /> Pray tarry with me this night. <break time="0.8s" /> For a lone woman is troubled. <break time="0.8s" /> With such all nights in the year. <break time="0.8s" /> This one night. <break time="0.8s" /> I must stay away from thee. <break time="0.8s" /> For my journey must be done. <break time="0.8s" /> Before sunrise. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he told her. <break time="0.8s" /> To say her prayers. <break time="0.8s" /> And go to bed at dusk. <break time="0.8s" /> Promising that no harm would come to her. <break Faith. <break time="0.8s" /> Still peeping after him. <break time="0.8s" /> With a melancholy air. <break time="0.8s" /> In spite of her pink ribbons. <break time="0.8s" /> What a wretch am I. <break <break time="0.8s" /> And follow her to heaven. <break time="0.8s" /> With this excellent resolve. <break time="0.8s" /> Goodman Brown hurried onward. <break time="0.8s" /> Along a dreary road. <break fearfully behind him. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking that someone might be hiding. <break time="0.8s" /> Behind every tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Or that the devil himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Might
